Merged to master (4b0755a). src/PyLOB/events.py: 7 frozen slotted dataclasses — 4 lifecycle (Accepted/Filled/Cancelled/Modified) + 3 configuration (SessionStarted/InstrumentConfigured/TraderConfigured). The config events are not in tasks.md but are REQUIRED: ADR-0001 says restart semantics come from the event log, and a fresh engine cannot reproduce commissions or balances from orders alone. KEY DECISIONS for downstream beads: (1) commissions compute IN THE CORE, not the sink — a sink is optional, so a required feature cannot live behind it; Filled carries both cumulative commission and the charged delta. (2) balances are DERIVED by the sink from a two-line rule in the module docstring, not evented. (3) seq and priority are separate counters; matching never reads seq, so a sinkless engine matches identically. (4) is_replayable() separates commands from consequences — Filled and IOC-remainder cancels are output the replayed engine re-derives. EventSink is a Protocol; close is optional via close_sink().

Merged to master (7ee1a46). src/PyLOB/sinks/sqlite.py — SQLiteSink, structurally conforming to events.EventSink and ClosableEventSink (verified). TWO-LAYER SCHEMA: append-only 'event' log (seq PK, kind, timestamp, replayable, JSON payload) + projections (session/instrument/trader/orders/trade/balance + resting_order and trader_commission views). Rationale: lob-5rt.7 needs an exact event stream (a projections-only schema forces replay to rebuild events, lossy the moment a projection summarises); lob-5rt.11 needs end-state comparison, for which the log is the wrong shape. The 'replayable' column is materialised by CALLING events.is_replayable, not by restating the rule in SQL. Commissions recorded not derived — the formula is absent from the file. Balances derived from the events docstring rule, quoted at the site. BUFFERING: consume() does one list append; batches flush as one transaction; orders stream written in strict seq order with runs of identical SQL coalesced so a Modified cannot clobber a later Filled; balance movements are incremental upserts so float summation order is independent of buffer_size (verified identical at 1/3/100000). Failed batch rolls back; poison batch dropped but remembered, and close() re-raises so a partial recording cannot report itself complete. For lob-5rt.7: use read_events(path, replayable_only=True) — do not write a second decoder or a second replayability rule.

Merged to master (57f6f7b). Structures: per side a dict of price levels + two lazily-deleted heaps (best-end and worst-end, sign-flipped). Best/worst price O(1) amortized, insert into existing level O(1), new level O(log L), cancel O(1). A level holds orders in an insertion-ordered dict keyed by idNum — it IS the FIFO queue but cancels in O(1) where design.md's deque would be O(N). Level volume cached incrementally. Measured 336k orders/sec for create+rest (target is 100x legacy's 439/s = 43.9k), ~7.6x headroom before matching and ledgers land. Identity by construction: lob-a17 (DuplicateOrderID on a supplied id already in the store), lob-7e7 (a supplied id pushes the counter past it, so replay re-seeds the counter from the stream with no separate restore step), lob-xqz (monotonic priority independent of timestamp and seq; verified identical with and without a sink), lob-ihv (InvalidOrder, not sys.exit). Quantization in decimal with half-even; every result verified an exact multiple of its tick including non-decimal ticks. No sqlite3 import (ADR-0001). LEFT TO 5rt.3: emission of Filled/Cancelled/Modified via the 'if book.recording: book.emit(...)' idiom so a sinkless engine never builds an event; setLastPrice exists but is uncalled; Order.value and Order.commission are declared and left at 0.0 for 5rt.5; BookSide.resize is the passive half of modify, the non-passive half is remove -> mutate price/priority -> add.

Merged to master (7d63369). Matching walks levels best-price-first, orders front-to-back within a level; (price, priority) is the entire sort, seq never read. Every fill prices at the maker. Market orders carry no price and their remainder is cancelled with IOC_REMAINDER; Order.resting is derived so 'never rests' is structural. SELF-MATCH GATE: steps OVER a gated order rather than removing it — keeps place, qty and fulfilled. Non-obvious problem solved: a fully gated best level would block the walk forever, so BookSide.match_levels lifts each price off the best-price heap before yielding its level and pushes back what the caller did not empty, driven under contextlib.closing so the restore always runs. Both sides fill through BookSide.fill because on a repriced modify the taker is itself in the book and its level's cached volume must stay honest. Closes lob-0bl on the new engine.

Merged to master (7d63369). Unknown identifier, wrong side, already-cancelled and nothing-left-to-cancel all raise PyLOBError subclasses; nothing changes before the last check passes, not even the clock. Quantity reduction clamps up to fulfilled. reprioritized = (price changed or qty increased); passive path uses BookSide.resize keeping queue place, non-passive is remove -> change -> re-stamp -> Modified -> match -> rest. Price comparison happens AFTER quantization, so modifying to the price an order already has stays passive. lob-crf DECISION: modifyOrder(price=None) means LEAVE THE PRICE UNCHANGED and crosses nothing — an order that named a limit keeps it until someone names a different one; a MISSING key raises InvalidOrder naming the field rather than a driver error. Verified: ask 5@105 resting, bid 5@99, modify(price=None) -> no trades, price still 99. Closes lob-0rb and lob-pn3 on the new engine.

Merged to master (7d63369). commission_for implements min(max_pct*V/100, max(min, per_unit*Q)) with the max INSIDE the min, so the percentage cap binds ahead of the floor. _charge recomputes from the order's cumulative (Q, V) and returns only the delta — cumulative recompute, not per-fill accrual. No round() anywhere in the module. Balances move by the events-module rule with no margin or funds check of any kind; an instrument with no declared currency moves only its own leg. Filled carries *_value, *_commission (cumulative) and *_commission_delta (increment) so the sink derives balances without re-deriving the formula. All 11 commissions and 9 trader-balances acceptance tests pass on the new engine.

Merged to master (cb27bd0). tests/test_sink_equality.py, 6 tests, 0.64s. This is the guarantee ADR-0002's workflow rests on — sinkless sweeps and recorded deep-dives must describe the same run. METHOD: not a shared seed, which is unsound here because the generator reads the book, so a divergence would change the operations themselves and each run would answer a different question. The first run RECORDS the concrete operations it performed and the second replays them verbatim. Stricter than a shared seed: an op names its target by identifier, so a run that assigned ids differently or filled an order the other left resting raises on the operation rather than sliding onto a different workload. The SINKLESS run goes first, mirroring the intended workflow. Compares queues in priority order, per-order state INCLUDING priority, money within 1e-9, all balances, last price, full trade sequence; plus a guard that the sink actually recorded (one 'accepted' per submission, one 'filled' per trade) so the comparison cannot be vacuous. NO DIVERGENCE across 5 seeds x 2000 ops. Mutation-verified: perturbing priority by seq fails all tests. FOUND AND FIXED (0539f77): SessionStarted was emitted ungated, so a sinkless engine built exactly one event — ADR-0002's 'no event at all' is now true as stated.

Merged to master (fdf5fd5 + 8cbffb1). flush() writes through the same path as consume and remembers what it lost; contract is 'raises iff events were lost'. A failed batch is SALVAGED one event at a time rather than dropped — equivalent to what a buffer_size=1 sink does with the same events, so it cannot produce a database the ordinary path could not; one poison event now costs one event, not 511. event_loss table + check_log (run by read_events) refuses a log with a loss row, a non-contiguous seq range, or an unknown stream/schema version. FOLLOW-UP ROUND closed the gap the first pass left: a KILLED process leaves an unflushed buffer, no loss row, contiguous survivors — so the log read as a complete shorter session. close() now writes a session_end row carrying the log's extent; a crash cannot forge it, so false positives are impossible and every false negative reads as unfinished. IncompleteLogError is distinct from corruption, corruption outranks it in check order, and the prefix stays readable via strict=False. That extent column also caught a hole NOBODY had flagged: rows deleted from the end of a FINISHED log leave seq contiguous and trip no marker. Agent also found and fixed a leak the review missed: the fold's currency memo survived a rolled-back write, denominating later fills in a currency the log cannot account for. Costs +4ns/event on the sink path, nothing sinkless, one COUNT(*) at close.

Merged to master (779134a). (a) configure_instrument currency withdrawal now RAISES rather than emitting — emitting was closed off by the sink (instrument.currency is NOT NULL, so the event would be a poison row salvaged into event_loss and the log would then refuse to read); also caught the empty-string path, which is falsy but not None and would have booked cash to a symbol named ''. (b) setLastPrice raises: book-queries defines last price as the most recent TRADE's price and requires a reload to agree with the persisted record, so an arbitrary setter contradicts the spec it mutates; _execute stays the only writer. If seeding an opening price matters, the alternative is a LastPriceSet event + one arm in the sink fold — flagged for maintainer decision. (c) match() AND rest() refuse an order the engine never registered, guarded on IDENTITY not membership so an impostor carrying a live idNum is refused too; rest() had the same hole and the bead had not named it. NOTHING PRIVATIZED — create_order/rest/match/emit/next_* carry 'not replay-coherent' notes and the privatization recommendation is written up for an ADR. DRIFT TEST built and verified as a detector (reverting setLastPrice and deleting a cancel emission made it name both): enumerates the public surface, derives each member's behaviour from observation, checks against a declared table with reasons; a new public method fails until classified. It found two things the bead missed: trader() registers a default schedule unrecorded (benign, documented) and book() creates a book for an unseen symbol (belongs to lob-kbx). One STRICT xfail records the deliberately-unfixed create_order replay incoherence. 301 passed / 14 xfailed; ~1% sinkless cost.

Resolved by ADR-0005 (7a1bc69), which supersedes ADR-0002. The >=100x target lost its denominator when ADR-0003 deleted the legacy engine, and a plain absolute floor would not have survived either: the 439/s figure never reproduced (the review re-measured the same legacy engine at 296/s), and the same sinkless workload ranged 49k-114k orders/sec inside one interleaved loop on this machine. So throughput is now judged against a CALIBRATION-NORMALISED baseline — a fixed reference computation of known cost runs alongside every benchmark, comparisons scale by the ratio of calibration figures, and a regression means the engine got more expensive relative to the machine it ran on. ADR-0002's substance survives (floor measured sinkless; sink-attached reported but not gating). 439/s is now a historical origin, not a live denominator. Also records that benchmark-harness's design decision 4 (--engine new|legacy) is void and its task 2.2 (legacy baselines) is unperformable — both to be reconciled at that change's archive.

Merged to master (ea1e675). Harness built per ADR-0005: seeded generators versioned by name (mixed-v1, checksum-pinned), runner with best-of-N and interleaving, baselines with tolerance and a deliberate --rebaseline that refuses on a non-quiet machine, and the calibration machinery. calib-v1 is five phases weighted to the engine's hot path with an AST test forbidding it to import the engine — if PyLOB.engine could move the denominator, a 30%-slower engine would slow the yardstick with it and read as no regression. DEMONSTRATED: across a load sweep on an UNCHANGED engine the raw figure called a regression at 4 of 6 levels; normalised called none, all exit 0. Paired: raw median 0.75 of unloaded with 9/10 below the floor, calibrated 0.91 with 0/10. Honest caveats recorded: calibrated estimators under-correct ~9% (60ms calibration pass is preempted less than a 110ms engine pass), and the work index was NOT shown to beat best-of-N (0.912 vs 0.915). NOT FIT FOR THE RECORDING RUN YET — an adversarial review found 3 P1s and a dozen P2s, all filed (lob-mk7, lob-vjq, lob-27r, lob-ta7); lob-lby.5 is now blocked on the P1s.

Merged to master (1ae6867). ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED all three. P1-A: the placeholder test asserted a project STATE not a system property; rewritten to 'either a marked placeholder or a complete record, never half of either'. Verified with a genuine harness-produced record (74 passed) and a malformed one (fails). Note my first verification attempt failed because I hand-built a record with guessed field names — the test correctly rejected it; using the harness to produce the record is the right method. Same class of bug found one layer down: a record missing its work index returned 'no baseline' = exit 0, silently disarming the guard. P1-B: interpreter identity (implementation, version, build) recorded and compared; mismatch = exit 3 rather than silent mis-judgement — the honest half, portability not claimed. P1-C: both signals now from the median (the statistic the verdict uses); a 94%-spread run that reported confident=True now reports False. The agent correctly REFUSED the brief on correlation: no single boolean can track normalisation error because nothing inside one run observes the true unloaded ratio, so it reports dispersion with numbers instead of a misleading boolean.

Merged to master (1ae6867). ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED the headline: fingerprints are now READ. Recorded a baseline, edited mixed-v1's passive depth without renaming (trades 1271 -> 796), re-ran -> 'INCOMPARABLE: the baseline measured a different order stream under the same name', EXIT 3. Restored the workload -> EXIT 0. Previously this reported ok/exit 0. compare() takes the fingerprints as REQUIRED arguments so forgetting is a TypeError. checksum=0 rejected in both registries. --rebaseline needs --rebaseline-down to move the floor down (--force deliberately does not carry it) and always prints the delta. Mislocated path / corrupt file / directory / invalid tolerance all exit 3, distinct from regression's 1. The 70/20/10 tests were tautologies (labels vs labels); realised mix measured through the engine is 57.6/32.4/10 and the CLAIM was corrected rather than the generator, since retuning means mixed-v2 and a re-baseline. NOT fixed, with reasons recorded: quiet-machine gate fails open on unknown power/load (tightening it risks blocking the very recording run this unblocks — separate decision); duty-cycle regressions and memory-bandwidth blindness need a change to what is measured, which is ADR-0005 territory.
